## ⛔ Read the triage grading before the body — it answered the question the body left open, and the answer inverts the repair

I filed this card reading the two docblocks as **ROTTED**. ⭐ **Triage measured it and I was wrong.** It read three converging sources — the `never` keys' own `@deprecated` lines, the maintainer ruling those keys were tombstoned under, and the fact that `spinner.tsx`'s own sentence already counts "beyond the SDUI base" and so was never counting `type` either — and concluded that a `never`-typed refusal is a **tombstone of an adjudicated-retired key, ⛔ not a declared key**.

⇒ **Both sentences are still TRUE today. ⛔ This is not ROTTED.**

⛔ Therefore: ⛔ no `⏱ DATED READING` block, ⛔ no falsifier, ⛔ no "true when written" preamble — that whole apparatus is for sentences that **became** false, and these did not. ⛔ And emphatically do **not** carry objectui#9753's BORN-FALSE correction repair across either; nothing here is being corrected.

## What lands

One sentence added to **each** of the two docblocks, making the **counting rule** explicit so the next reader does not have to re-derive it: what "declares exactly" counts is the keys an **author can write and the renderer can receive**; a `never`-typed refuse-by-name is a tombstone of a retired key and is not counted. Point at that key's own `@deprecated` line and at the ruling's provenance rather than restating them.

⛔ Triage deliberately did not dictate the wording, and neither do I. ⛔ Do not turn this into a rewrite of either docblock — one sentence each, and nothing else moves.

## ⚠️ The exit channel — ⛔ you do not adjudicate this yourself

If you find, in **governed text** (a pin ledger, ADR-0049's counting rule, anything of that standing), a line that explicitly **does** count a `never` key as a declared member, then both sentences are FALSE, this card flips to **ROTTED at p2**, and the repair inverts to the dating one.

⇒ At that moment: **STOP.** ⛔ Do not write either repair. Hand back, and the card goes to `pm:retriage` with the objection in the same write. ⛔ Never settle a counting rule from the dev seat.

## Why this is worth doing at p3

⭐ It has a **named live reader**: PR objectui#9763 just repointed a changeset paragraph at these two docblocks as its evidence that each renderer consumes its own node's keys by name. So "nobody is reading this file" does not hold, and the Acceptance-notes fallback is unavailable.

⭐ And the line worth keeping in view while you write: both sentences say **"MEASURED, not assumed"**. They have not gone stale — but nothing would fire if they did. That is the family this card belongs to.

**File surface:** `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/icon.tsx` and `packages/components/src/renderers/feedback/spinner.tsx`, plus a changeset.

**Serial constraint:** re-take over the open-PR 全集 immediately before your first write, ⛔ not this round's branches.

⛔ **`Fixes #9764`** is correct here **only** if you deliver both sentences and nothing is left; otherwise `Refs` and say what remains.

## 1. ⛔ THE EXIT-CHANNEL RULING — the one thing this hand-back needed from me

The dev found `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md` labelling ADR-0049 tombstones **`DECLARED but UNWRITABLE`**, reported it as the nearest miss, and ⛔ correctly did not decide it. I read it and rule: **the exit channel is NOT triggered.**

Triage's condition is worded **明确把 `never` 键算作 declared member** — *explicitly counts*. Read whole, that line does the opposite:

```
// ADR-0049 RETIREMENT TOMBSTONES (objectui#5905) - DECLARED but UNWRITABLE.
// Every key named here is `never` on the published type, so authoring one is a
// `tsc` error and a named refusal from the Zod mirror (`ComponentInputSchema`).
// They were never read and never published: the manifest serializer forwards
// only `name`, `type`, `required`, `enum`, `binding` and `description`, so an
// authored value was silently dropped.
```

⭐ **It is a contrast construction, and the contrast is the counting rule stated from the other side.** "DECLARED **but** UNWRITABLE" only earns its `but` if "declared" alone would mislead someone into thinking the key is usable — and the five lines under it spend their whole length saying it is not: a `tsc` error to author, refused by name, never read, never published, silently dropped. ⇒ it uses "declared" as a bare type-level fact and then warns against exactly the inference the docblock rule excludes.

And mechanically: it states **no count**, adjudicates **no** "declares exactly" sentence, and names a different type (`ComponentInput`, a plugin manifest descriptor) than either schema here.

⇒ ⛔ Not a counting rule. Card does ⛔ not flip to ROTTED, ⛔ does not go to p2, ⛔ does not go to `pm:retriage`. This PR's repair stands. ⭐ Reporting it rather than deciding it was the right call, and I would rather see ten of those than one silently-settled 口径.

## 2. Triage's three readings — and the dev extended one past triage

Re-taken by me on `origin/main`:

- The family-D pin `packages/types/src/__tests__/content-channel-family-d-9256.test.ts` exists, names both schemas, and carries the ruling verbatim: `(maintainer ruling, summon #17 decision batch #2, 2026-09-07, …)`.
- ⭐ **`packages/types/src/feedback.ts` carries that citation ZERO times; `layout.ts` carries it seven.** That is why both added sentences point at the **pin** rather than at "the same file" — pointing `spinner.tsx` at its own file's ruling citation would have been a dead pointer. Good catch, and I verified it rather than take it.
- The dev extended triage's self-counting argument from `spinner` to `icon`, **as a measurement**: at `e304a4ef7`, `IconSchema` already declared `type` beside `icon`/`size`/`color` while the sentence said three. ⇒ its unit was never "interface member declaration", before any `never` key existed. I confirmed that reading earlier today from the same ref. ⭐ That is the strongest leg of the three, and it is the dev's, not triage's.

## 3. The diff

One sentence added per docblock, nothing else moved. Each **names the rule** and copies no member list — the self-defeating alternative in a card about written-down member lists. Each says "not counted", never "not declared", which is the honest distinction: the key **is** on the type; it is not in what the sentence counts.

Empty-frontmatter changeset, grade **measured from a build** of `@object-ui/components`: across the 212 files of the published surface the added prose reads 0, pre-existing docblock prose from the same two files also reads 0, against live controls reading 3 and 5 on the same instrument and corpus. ⇒ the comment channel reaches no published byte.

`Fixes #9764` correct — both sentences delivered, nothing left over. `Clause-②: no`.

## 4. The pending-changeset re-read the gate asked for — answered, and the interesting one is the second

- `.changeset/5632-…` — **did not go false.** Its pointers into both docblocks still resolve, now to docblocks that also state the counting rule.
- `.changeset/5993-…` — ⭐ **its final paragraph IS false today, and ⛔ not because of this PR.** Measured at the write-time ref `194fae184`: the file *did* then carry its own `toPascalCase` + `iconNameMap` + `icons[...]`. ⇒ **ROTTED**, and the falsifier is `e176053094` (the seven-resolvers-to-one seam), ⛔ not this diff — the "is untouched" half is scoped to objectui#5993's own change, so a later touch does not falsify it.

⭐ **Naming this PR as the falsifier would have been writing a false repair**, and the dev saw that and filed nothing. That is the correct instinct on a card whose whole subject is provenance. Filed by the seat as a successor — see below.

## 5. ⛔ MY OWN DEFECT, caught by this dev's tooling run

`check-clause2-carriers --pair 9770` exited **4**: my claim comment's keys were composed from memory as decorated markdown rows (`- **Clause-②:** …`) instead of copied from the template's literal spelling, so the gate could read **none** of them — including the claim's own id, which is why the correction comment I posted first could not be matched to anything.

Repaired by editing the claim comment to the template's literal shape (⛔ never a second `Claim:`, which the protocol forbids), with the edit and its reason declared in the comment itself; `Container & model` left marked **NOT MEASURED** rather than filled in, because repairing a line's spelling ⛔ does not license adding a reading that was never taken. The same defect was repaired on card objectui#8071's slice-11 claim **before** its PR opens. Re-run: **exit 0**.

⚠️ And that pass message asserts something false — that the claim was not edited, when `updated_at` ≠ `created_at` on the very object the script already reads. Filed as **objectstack#18892**.
